'''''Ficus lyrata''''', commonly known as the '''fiddle-leaf fig''', '''banjo fig''', '''fiddle-leaved fig tree''', '''lyre leaf fig tree''', or '''lyre-leaved fig tree''', is a species of plant in the mulberry and fig family [[Moraceae]]. It is [[native species|native]] to western Africa, but is cultivated around the world as an ornamental plant.<ref name=IUCN/><ref name=CABI>{{cite report |last1=Datiles |first1=M. J. |last2=Acevedo-Rodrígue |first2=P. |title=''Ficus lyrata'' |date=7 January 2022 |doi=10.1079/cabicompendium.24125 |doi-access=free }}</ref> <ref>{{cite web
 |title=The History of Fiddle Leaf Fig Plants
 |url=https://houseplantresourcecenter.com/blogs/news/the-history-of-fiddle-leaf-fig-plants
 |website=Houseplant Resource Center
 |access-date=10 June 2026
}}</ref> It has received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name=AGM>{{cite web |title=Ornamental AGM Plants April 2023 |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |date=April 2023 |publisher=[[Royal Horticultural Society]] |page=46 |access-date=20 January 2024}}</ref>

==Description==
''Ficus lyrata'' is an evergreen tree or shrub, native to the tropical rain forests of West and Central Africa, and is one of the most demanding and showy ''Ficus'' species. Outdoors, it can grow {{Convert|9-12|m|abbr=on}} tall.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Bercu |first1=Rodica |title=ANATOMICAL ASPECTS OF FICUS LYRATA WARB. (MORACEAE) LEAF |journal=Annals of West University of Timisoara: Series of Biology |date=2015 |volume=18 |issue=2 |pages=107–114 |id={{ProQuest|1751976433}} |url=https://biologie.uvt.ro/annals/vol_18_2/AWUTSerBio_December2015_107-114.pdf }}</ref>

The [[leaf|leaves]] are variable in shape, but often with a broad apex and narrow middle, resembling a [[lyre]] or [[fiddle]]; they are up to {{convert|45|cm|in|abbr=on|0}} long and {{convert|30|cm|in|abbr=on|0}} broad (though usually smaller), with a leathery texture, prominent veins and a wavy margin.

The [[fruit]] is a green fig {{Convert|2.5-3|cm|4=1|abbr=on}} diameter.

==Distribution and habitat==
''F. lyrata'' is native to [[Benin]], [[Cameroon]], [[Gabon]], [[Ghana]], [[Guinea]], [[Guinea-Bissau]], [[Ivory Coast]], [[Liberia]], [[Nigeria]], [[Sierra Leone]], and [[Togo]], where it occurs in moist lowland forests. It also occurs as an [[introduced species]] in the [[Canary Islands]], [[El Salvador]], and [[Trinidad and Tobago]].<ref name=IUCN/><ref name=powo/>
<gallery>
Ficus lyrata 393081768.jpg|''Ficus lyrata'' leaves are [[lyrate]], meaning that they resemble a lyre.
Ficus lyrata - fruit (Gardenology.org).jpg|The fruit is a green fig.
</gallery>

==Cultivation==
It is widely grown outdoors in tropical regions, and also as a decorative species indoors in Europe and North America. During the 2010s, it became increasingly popular as a houseplant and interior design feature.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=The History of Fiddle Leaf Fig Plants
 |url=https://houseplantresourcecenter.com/blogs/news/the-history-of-fiddle-leaf-fig-plants
 |website=Houseplant Resource Center
 |access-date=10 June 2026
}}</ref> It is a popular [[ornamental tree]] in subtropical and tropical gardens, and is also grown as a [[houseplant]] in [[temperateness|temperate]] areas, where it usually stays shorter and fails to flower or fruit. It thrives in bright, indirect light and can tolerate some direct sunlight. It is hardy down to {{convert|10|C|F|abbr=on}}, so specimens may be placed outside during warm periods.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ficus lyrata (Banjo fig, Fiddle-leaf Fig) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/ficus-lyrata/ |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref>

=== Propagation ===
''Ficus lyrata'' can be propagated by division, stem cuttings, or air layering.<ref name=":0" />
